verses.text: Now when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the royal offspring.

But Jehosheba, the daughter of king Joram, sister of Ahaziah, took Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stole him away from among the king’s sons who were slain, even him and his nurse, and put them in the bedroom; and they hid him from Athaliah, so that he was not slain.
He was with her hidden in Yahweh’s house six years while Athaliah reigned over the land.

In the seventh year Jehoiada sent and fetched the captains over hundreds of the Carites and of the guard, and brought them to him into Yahweh’s house; and he made a covenant with them, and made a covenant with them in Yahweh’s house, and showed them the king’s son.
He commanded them, saying, “This is what you must do: a third of you, who come in on the Sabbath, shall be keepers of the watch of the king’s house;
a third of you shall be at the gate Sur; and a third of you at the gate behind the guard. So you shall keep the watch of the house, and be a barrier.
The two companies of you, even all who go out on the Sabbath, shall keep the watch of Yahweh’s house around the king.
You shall surround the king, every man with his weapons in his hand; and he who comes within the ranks, let him be slain. Be with the king when he goes out, and when he comes in.”

The captains over hundreds did according to all that Jehoiada the priest commanded; and they each took his men, those who were to come in on the Sabbath, with those who were to go out on the Sabbath, and came to Jehoiada the priest.
The priest delivered to the captains over hundreds the spears and shields that had been king David’s, which were in Yahweh’s house.
The guard stood, every man with his weapons in his hand, from the right side of the house to the left side of the house, along by the altar and the house, around the king.
Then he brought out the king’s son, and put the crown on him, and gave him the covenant; and they made him king, and anointed him; and they clapped their hands, and said, “Long live the king!”
When Athaliah heard the noise of the guard and of the people, she came to the people into Yahweh’s house:

and she looked, and behold, the king stood by the pillar, as the tradition was, with the captains and the trumpets by the king; and all the people of the land rejoiced, and blew trumpets. Then Athaliah tore her clothes, and cried, “Treason! Treason!”

Jehoiada the priest commanded the captains of hundreds who were set over the army, and said to them, “Bring her out between the ranks. Kill anyone who follows her with the sword.” For the priest said, “Don’t let her be slain in Yahweh’s house.”
So they made way for her; and she went by the way of the horses’ entry to the king’s house, and she was slain there.
Jehoiada made a covenant between Yahweh and the king and the people, that they should be Yahweh’s people; also between the king and the people.

All the people of the land went to the house of Baal, and broke it down; his altars and his images broke they in pieces thoroughly, and killed Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars. The priest appointed officers over Yahweh’s house.

He took the captains over hundreds, and the Carites, and the guard, and all the people of the land; and they brought down the king from Yahweh’s house, and came by the way of the gate of the guard to the king’s house. He sat on the throne of the kings.
So all the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet. They had slain Athaliah with the sword at the king’s house.
Jehoash was seven years old when he began to reign.

footnotes.content: The fear in Athaliah's heart runs so deep she destroys her own grandchildren—all to hold onto a throne she never had a rightful claim to begin with. Power seized by violence always hungers for more blood; it can never rest.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: What courage in a woman's heart—Jehosheba reaches into the chaos and pulls out life. She hides the boy in plain sight, in the house of God itself, where a murderous queen cannot touch him. The Lord often works through quiet defiance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Six years Joash grows in hiding, while outside the temple walls, a usurper claims the throne. Even in darkness, even when the world looks lost, the Lord is preparing His purposes. The hidden years are never wasted.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jehoiada the priest gathers the captains—the men who hold real power—and brings them into the temple to see the boy. A covenant made here, in God's house, will break a kingdom's grip. Truth spoken in the sanctuary carries weight.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Every third man stands watch, rotating so none grow weary. Jehoiada builds discipline into the plan—not rushing, not relying on fervor alone, but steady faithfulness. Lasting freedom requires patient, methodical preparation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The gates are positioned, the watch divided—three points of strength holding the line. Jehoiada thinks like a shepherd protecting the flock, posting guards where danger enters. The Lord trains our hands for what matters most.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All who leave and all who return—both movements guarded. The priest leaves nothing to chance. I've learned this from Scripture: when we step out in faith, God honors detail and care just as much as boldness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Be with the king when he goes out, and when he comes in." The guards form a human shield, weapons ready. To stand near someone who is vulnerable, to put your own body between them and harm—this is the shape of faithfulness in hard times.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The captains do exactly as commanded—no hesitation, no arguing about the plan. When people trust their leader, especially a priest they know walks with God, obedience becomes almost easy. Authority rooted in faith carries its own authority.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jehoiada brings out the spears and shields of King David—holy relics now pressed into service to protect David's line. What once guarded the kingdom in its glory now defends a hidden child. History keeps its old wounds and old faithfulness both.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Every man armed, standing shoulder to shoulder from right side to left—a wall of steel around a seven-year-old boy. Sometimes the Lord's protection comes through human hands and human courage, standing firm until the moment of revelation arrives.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The crown goes on the boy's head, the covenant placed in his hands, and the people clap and shout. After six years of hiding, suddenly the name of the king is spoken aloud again. The Lord knows His timing; what was impossible becomes inevitable.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Athaliah hears the noise and comes running to the temple. A usurper's confidence crumbles the moment she hears truth spoken openly. Lies always fear the light; kingdoms built on blood shake at the sound of an honest cry.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: She sees the boy standing by the pillar—the rightful king has been crowned while she ruled. Her clothes torn, crying "Treason!"—but the treason was hers all along. Sometimes what feels like the end of the world is only the end of a lie.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jehoiada will not let her die in the temple—mercy even in judgment, even for an enemy who showed none. The house of God is a place of holiness, not bloodletting. Truth stands firm without needing to be vicious.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They escort her out and she meets her end at the horses' gate. The threat is removed, the kingdom cleansed of its usurper. What seemed untouchable is humbled in a moment when the Lord's timing arrives.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jehoiada makes a covenant binding the king, the priest, and the people together in Yahweh's sight. All three—ruler, spiritual leader, and people—bound under God. This is what a kingdom looks like when it remembers who it truly serves.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The people tear down Baal's house and smash his altars to pieces—a swift, thorough cleansing. When the Lord restores His kingdom, false worship cannot coexist with true faith. The idols have to go; the people know this in their bones.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The boy is brought down from the temple to the royal house, escorted through the city as the king he always was. Seven years old, sitting on the throne of his fathers—a child, yet held steady by priests and captains who remember God's law.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The city becomes quiet—no more fear, no more the shadow of a usurper's reign. Readers today hear an echo in that quietness: the deep peace that comes when truth finally speaks openly and the kingdom remembers its true king. Even now, tired souls long for that kind of rest.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Seven years old when he begins to reign—barely past babyhood, yet the Lord steadies his reign through faithful priests and returning people. Sometimes the kingdom's greatest hope comes not from might, but from a child cradled in the arms of those who love God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
